method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, reconstruction of the compactness argument and contradiction proof, and exact formula, macro, controlled-token, identifier and reference comparison. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: The overspill consequence from arbitrarily large finite models to an infinite model, and the resulting non-definability of infinitude by one first-order sentence.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If a sentence set has finite models of unbounded size, it has an infinite model. Add countably many distinct constants; every finite part is satisfiable because a sufficiently large finite model exists, so compactness gives a model satisfying all pairwise inequalities and hence having an infinite domain.
samples.checks: The unbounded finite-size quantifiers, countable constant family, finite-satisfiability step, compactness use and final distinctness argument are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: No sentence in any first-order language is true exactly in structures with infinite domain. Otherwise its negation would have every finite structure and no infinite structure as a model, contradicting the preceding overspill theorem.
samples.checks: The quantification over all first-order languages, biconditional domain condition, negation move, exact finite/infinite model contrast and theorem reference are retained.
